idea: An old watchmaker holds up a stopped pocket watch in his dim workshop. He says quietly: "It stopped in 1987, at 3:15 a.m., and so did I."

script.title: Frozen Time
script.logline: An aging watchmaker confronts a lifetime of suspended grief while clutching a pocket watch that stopped decades ago.
script.setting: Dim, dust-mote-filled horology workshop crowded with antique clock pendulums, brass gears, and warm amber workbench lamplight.

characters.name: Arthur
characters.look: Late-seventies craftsman with deep crow's feet, wispy white comb-over hair, wearing a threadbare tweed vest over a rolled-sleeve canvas shirt, with a thick magnifying jeweler's loupe resting on his furrowed forehead.
characters.voiceDescription: Husky rasping older male voice, late-70s, weary British accent, slow and reflective.

shots.visual: Arthur sits beneath a warm desk lamp, gently raising a tarnished silver pocket watch beside his cheek, his solemn gaze fixed on the frozen clock face.
shots.motion: Slow push-in toward Arthur as he lifts the watch into the amber lamplight.
shots.line: It stopped in 1987, at 3:15 a.m., and so did I.
shots.speaker: Arthur

shots.visual: Tight on Arthur's weathered face as his calloused thumb gently traces the cracked crystal face of the pocket watch, eyes glistening under the faint light.
shots.motion: Subtle handheld drift lingering on Arthur's damp eyes and trembling chin.

quotedLines: It stopped in 1987, at 3:15 a.m., and so did I.
